item.title: Instagram Rolls out an AI Video Assistant for Creators (1 minute read)
item.description: Instagram is rolling out an AI video assistant in Edits, its CapCut competitor, that gives creators personalized feedback instead of generic advice. The assistant combines account metrics like views and video retention with comments and trends to spot performance patterns, while leaving creative calls to creators. Usage is capped, with more available through a Meta One subscription.

item.title: The New Firefox Design: More Modern, More Flexible, Still Firefox (2 minute read)
item.description: Mozilla is rolling out the Firefox 157 redesign to all desktop and mobile users, refreshing colors, icons, and themes across the browser without hurting performance. The update adds flexibility through a returning Compact Mode, a theme picker with new themes and wallpapers, and a customizable New Tab page with pinned shortcuts. Firefox remains independent and open source, with built-in privacy protections and user controls, including over AI features, since the redesign renews rather than reinvents it.

item.title: John Ternus has big plans to make Apple ‘leaner' and release more products (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple CEO John Ternus reportedly wants a leaner organization focused on engineering, with fewer management layers and more frequent product releases. Apple has dismissed some engineering program managers, while Ternus is considering a less seasonal launch schedule and more experimental products. The plans also include growing services revenue through new offerings and existing products.

item.title: Has Your Product Outgrown its Floor Plan? (6 minute read)
item.description: Visual inconsistency gets the attention, but spatial incoherence is often worse, as products expand past the simple floor plan they launched with. Slack's pile of added features and Substack's inconsistent reader and publisher navigation show the problem, while YouTube's clearly scoped menus make shifts easy to map. Overlays that misrepresented an action's scope were one reason Shopify deprecated its Polaris Sheet component, forcing a rethink of the admin's floor plan.

item.title: How to De-slopify Your Designs (8 minute read)
item.description: Vibecoders can keep AI-generated designs from looking like generic slop by learning to spot its telltale components, then applying one of three escalating fixes: cleaning up fluff with specific colors, fonts, and icons; defining an aesthetic through references; or designing from scratch in Figma. Since slop stems from generating artifacts without thought or effort, even a brief review forces reflection, and AI handles digital styles far better than organic, expressive ones. These levels suit one-off designs like dashboards and trivia decks, while fixing an entire product or brand would require agentic workflows and design systems.

item.title: A design system is what it does (6 minute read)
item.description: Matt Henry argues that a design system's defaults reveal which users and tasks it prioritizes, comparing the US Web Design System (USWDS) with shadcn. USWDS supports information-heavy government websites through readable typography and guidance that explains its design choices, while shadcn's denser defaults require more customization. He warns that a possible shift from USWDS to shadcn could make public information less accessible, especially when government teams lack the time or expertise to adjust those defaults.

item.title: Murri unveils RCD Espanyol de Barcelona brand identity (3 minute read)
item.description: Murri's refreshed identity for RCD Espanyol de Barcelona preserves the soccer club's history while creating a more flexible visual system for modern applications. Custom Perico Type typography draws on Catalan poster traditions and the club's blue-and-white stripes, supported by graphic elements derived from its visual heritage. The system is designed to work consistently across stadium environments, digital platforms, merchandise, and communications while keeping the club's established identity recognizable.

item.title: Building an Independent Design Practice (5 minute read)
item.description: More than 10,000 hours of independent design work produce five lessons, from following what gives energy to testing through moonlighting first. Saying yes early builds stability and reveals where skills meet demand, while the clients a practice wants to attract shape its pricing. Starting most engagements with a couple of weeks on a well-scoped project lets both sides experience the relationship before committing.

item.title: What Happens When You Can Build It All Yourself (8 minute read)
item.description: Building everything alone with AI agents got a complex backend to alpha in under two weeks, and the bar for normal output keeps rising. Within weeks came a new Noord site, the Vlak design system with 200-plus components, the Bureau workspace for people and AI agents, and three workbooks. Unless a software startup is doing frontier work, most of the money it raises should go toward discovering or building distribution channels rather than product development.

item.title: Designer Steven Haulenbeek Turns Functional Objects into Physical Records of Ice, Sand, Fire, and Serendipity (1 minute read)
item.description: Carved ice, molten bronze, and reclaimed foundry sand let industrial designer Steven Haulenbeek make furniture and lighting shaped by weather, gravity, heat, and chance.

item.title: Louise French quit London, cycled the Andes and came home an illustrator (7 minute read)
item.description: After leaving London and cycling through South America, Louise French renewed her illustration practice, developing a playful style through drawing and the freedom to experiment.

item.title: You Can Now Use ChatGPT and Claude to Speed up 3D Art in Cinema 4D (2 minute read)
item.description: Maxon's Cinema 4D now lets artists direct Claude, ChatGPT, or Codex through a built-in MCP server, automating repetitive tasks with natural language instructions.

item.title: Midjourney Adds Live Style Previews and More Reversible Controls (1 minute read)
item.description: Midjourney added live style previews in the Styles sidebar, saved prompt defaults, and undo for project deletion. Experimental previews rely on fast models and prompt text alone, and picking a style submits the prompt with it. Midjourney says its updated edit model preserves pixels outside the selected area, a claim shown only in an official demonstration, not an independent test.

item.title: Apple's HomePad smart home hub launching on Oct 13 with iMac G4 design (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's long-awaited HomePad smart home hub is reportedly launching October 13 with a 6-inch display and a design inspired by the iconic iMac G4. The device is expected to combine a speaker and smart home control panel with a new operating system drawing on iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, centered around Siri AI. Two versions have reportedly been developed: a tabletop model and another designed to mount on a wall.

item.title: Figma Invests in the UK with Expanded London Office (2 minute read)
item.description: Figma has expanded its London office at Elder Yard on Norton Folgate, deepening investment in one of its largest markets outside the United States. Two thirds of the FTSE 100 build with Figma as of Q2 2026, and over 15 million files were created in the UK in the past year. Figma's global AI report found 41% of product builders say AI meaningfully changes team collaboration, and 52% of UK respondents now say design matters more.

item.title: How AI Agents Are Reshaping UX (3 minute read)
item.description: Decagon CEO Jesse Zhang says personal AI agents such as Meta's Muse will reshape customer experience, since agents skip product displays and purchase-inducing flows. Amazon blocked Muse while Shopify opened a dedicated payment channel, though Zhang expects Amazon to back down because customers want AI assistant integration. Companies need to verify agent authority, set negotiation limits, handle exceptions, and stop fraud running at machine speed, with AI systems ultimately transacting machine to machine.

item.title: What Does AI-Readiness Mean in Design Systems? (7 minute read)
item.description: AI-ready design systems depend less on specialized agent tooling and more on strong engineering fundamentals that make components, APIs, tokens, and documentation easy for machines to discover and understand. Testing with the Open Design System Bench found that clean separation of concerns and a single source of truth can outperform additional instruction files, which may actually hurt results when they contain stale or duplicated information. Mechanical correctness is only half the challenge: design systems also need principles and guidance that help AI exercise good design judgment rather than simply generate technically valid interfaces.

item.title: The Box Design System: AI‑Ready Figma Files for Enterprise Software (8 minute read)
item.description: Flexy Global's Box Design System organizes complex enterprise product behavior into bounded Figma sections, making design files easier for people to navigate and for AI coding agents to use. Boxes form a feature, flow, and screen-state hierarchy built around behavior rather than pages, with self-contained context and arrows showing transitions. They cannot fix an undefined product or replace the design system and codebase, but as design files become inputs to AI-assisted development, this structure is becoming part of the product.

item.title: amazing-glass (Website)
item.description: Amazing Glass provides framework-independent web components that recreate Apple-style Liquid Glass using physically inspired refraction, interactive controls, and pixel-level comparisons against Apple's SwiftUI renderer rather than relying on simple backdrop blur.

item.description: Run every brand shoot with confidence. From moodboards and shot lists to call sheets and shoot day, walk onto set knowing nothing was missed.

item.description: The Last Museum is a semantic search engine for 6.3 million artworks from the world's great museums.

item.title: A Short Update on Designing for Foldable Devices (1 minute read)
item.description: Three years after the Google Pixel Fold, the iPhone Duo announcement brings a fresh look at designing for foldable devices. CSS media features, a Viewport Segments API, and a Device Posture API work only in Chromium browsers, with no sign yet of Safari support. Websites needn't adapt to two screens. A dual-screen design makes sense when an experience has two simultaneous contexts, such as an inbox beside an open message.

item.title: Do Product Designers Need UI/UX Skills? (6 minute read)
item.description: Product designers do need UI/UX skills, because product design spans research, wireframes, prototypes, testing, and developer collaboration, and UI/UX principles apply at nearly every stage. UI covers what users see, while UX covers whether the product works, and a beautiful app nobody can figure out still fails. Designers need not master every corner, but skills in research, wireframing, prototyping, and usability testing help them read user behavior accurately and keep decisions grounded.

item.title: This packaging for ready-made dinners can teach you to cook better (4 minute read)
item.description: Center's identity for chef Daniel Humm's Riff turns ready-to-cook meal packaging into a lightweight cooking lesson, showing optional fresh ingredients alongside explanations of how each changes a dish's flavor. The visual system combines a chunky curved wordmark, 12 food-inspired colors, three contrasting typefaces, deliberately unstyled food photography, and a playful mascot called Dan the Pan. Packaging reinforces the idea of improvisation with cooking tips, recipe variations, and QR codes linking to Humm's cooking videos, positioning convenience food as a starting point for learning rather than a finished product.

item.title: MoMA Explores the Useful Beauty of Information Design (3 minute read)
item.description: MoMA's exhibit Full Disclosure: The Edge of Information Design, which opened September 27, is the museum's first devoted entirely to information design.

item.title: Genius 'Tilted' Apple Watch Band Makes the Entire Experience 10x More Ergonomic (2 minute read)
item.description: A Tilted Watch Band angles the Apple Watch 30 degrees so the screen faces the wearer without a horizontal wrist, easing strain on the wrist and neck.

item.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its bubbly agentic avatar (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI has launched Dots, always-on personal agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that pursue user-defined goals in the background rather than staying tied to a single interface. Available to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets, Dots can be launched from ChatGPT or Codex and contacted through platforms such as Slack and Teams, with text messaging planned. Their floating, cartoon-like avatars give autonomous software a more approachable identity, while OpenAI envisions specialist Dots working together with their own tools and permissions.

item.title: You'll either love or hate the Formula E logo – and that's the whole point (3 minute read)
item.description: Formula E's new identity by MOX centers on a deliberately divisive logomark that combines an F and E at a 30-degree angle to convey speed and momentum. A bespoke type family based on AP Gavel expands the system with condensed italics for energy and a monospaced style for technical data, complemented by Inter for longer copy. Surge Purple, Signal Orange, and Electric Lime add a distinctive palette designed to give the championship a more expressive identity as it enters its GEN4 era.

item.title: Replit Acquires Atta to Bring AI Business Analysis into Its Platform (2 minute read)
item.description: Replit has acquired Atta, an AI-powered business analysis workspace, bringing its data-analysis and charting technology directly into Replit's platform. Users can upload or connect a dataset and ask Replit Agent to investigate a question or generate a visualization without writing SQL. The move reflects a broader shift toward folding business analysis into the same environment used to build and operate software.

item.title: Don't forget to design (4 minute read)
item.description: Design isn't something that happens after fully understanding a problem. Making sketches and prototypes is itself a way to discover what the problem really is. Rough ideas expose gaps, tensions, and requirements that research, data, and discussion alone may never reveal. An excessive focus on outcomes can discourage designers from making anything, even though reaching a good outcome often requires producing and evaluating lots of imperfect work along the way.

item.title: The Fastest Gun in UX: Why Your Team is Telling the Wrong Story (5 minute read)
item.description: Designers are rushing through their process to prove value through speed, but the real contest is winning stakeholder alignment, where they are both vulnerable and well positioned. The "Fastest Gun in the West" hijacks planning by anchoring early on an idea, using vague agile language, and pressuring designers to produce polished mockups that lock in unexamined assumptions while research is dismissed as slow. Since designers can't outrun someone shooting from the hip, they should use low-fidelity tools like scenario storyboards and PRFAQs to engage stakeholders on mental models and outcomes.

item.title: Skip the Tools, Make the Outcomes (3 minute read)
item.description: AI creates opportunities to skip traditional tools and deliver the outcomes those tools were originally designed to help people achieve. An AI-powered newsroom called Exposit discovered that users overwhelmingly preferred asking for a topic and receiving a personalized, up-to-date report instead of navigating headlines, categories, and search interfaces. This “outcome first, tool second” approach suggests a useful product design question: whether a new AI experience needs another interface at all, or can simply produce what people came for.

item.title: Crafting WCAG 3 for More Accessible User Experiences (5 minute read)
item.description: WCAG 3's September 2026 draft sets a single conformance level, called core requirements, built on WCAG 2.2's Level A and AA success criteria. Supplemental requirements, assertions, and recommended practices cover accessibility needs that can't be objectively measured or don't apply everywhere, encouraging organizations to go beyond the baseline. Tags let regulators tailor requirements to specific situations and let websites report progress toward and beyond conformance, with multiple reporting tiers built in.

item.title: Best AI Image Models 2026: Tested by Human Evaluators (10 minute read)
item.description: Everypixel's blind evaluation of 863 pairwise judgments across 48 commercial scenes found no universal winner among 2026's leading AI image models. GPT Image 2 showed the strongest evidence for high-precision commercial generation and controlled photorealism, though its direct comparison against real photography wasn't statistically conclusive. Qwen Image 2 suits controlled editing, Nano Banana 2 fast iteration, Nano Banana Pro consistency, Grok Imagine creative interpretation, and FLUX.2 an explore-then-finish workflow.

item.description: Hong Kong-based illustrator Brian Yuen paints in Photoshop with a style drawn from the Old Masters and artists like Jaime Jones and Craig Mullins.

item.description: Apple in Colour is an interactive archive from sheets.works that brings together 341 Apple product colors spanning nearly three decades, from the Bondi Blue iMac to recent iPhones, complete with release years and official color names.

item.title: This Advent Calendar is Filled with Design-Led Gifts (1 minute read)
item.description: Westwing's 2026 advent calendar comes in an oversized house-shaped box illustrated by Munich-based artist Kera Till, with 24 doors hiding home decor, tableware, and self-care pieces.

item.title: Artists, Game Designers and Producers Hit Hard as Microsoft Cuts 277 Jobs in Washington State (1 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft cut 277 jobs in the Seattle region, according to a newly public WARN Act filing, with artists, game designers and producers among the hardest hit. Art, production, design, and audio roles total 77 positions, while software engineering is the largest single category at 60. Of the cuts, 252 were at the Redmond campus, and 25 were remote, part of a wider Xbox restructuring that also moves the next Halo game to Activision.

item.title: YouTube Releases New AI Features for Creators within its Studio App (2 minute read)
item.description: YouTube is adding AI tools to its Studio app that critique unpublished videos on pacing, structure, and storytelling before creators publish. A new research feed shows what content performs well on the platform, and thumbnails and titles can be generated to match a creator's own style. Creators have already run over 40 million title and thumbnail A/B tests, and Studio will soon test three video cuts and swap out weak thumbnails automatically.

item.title: Apple's XR headset plans are supposedly on life support, as it experiments with new design ideas (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple is exploring a completely redesigned Vision headset that could address the Vision Pro's biggest weakness—its weight—using lighter materials or moving the processor and battery into a separate puck similar to Meta's new VR glasses. Several concepts are reportedly under consideration, but development remains uncertain, and any new headset is unlikely to arrive before 2028 or 2029.

item.title: The 5 Big Lessons Designers Must Learn (3 minute read)
item.description: Five lessons run through design work: someone always has to pay for an idea, and framing it as higher quality sells better than calling it good design. Power, not talent, decides most projects, since whoever controls budget, schedule, and goals is the real designer, leaving others to work through influence instead. What counts as good depends on context, such as affordability and bureaucracy, and products bought before they're used are often designed to sell rather than to serve.

item.title: How to Sync a Design System with Claude Design (17 minute read)
item.description: Syncing a design system with Claude Design creates a mirror: a compiled, self-rendering copy of the component library, so Claude designs with the real components. The sync runs with /design-sync from Claude Code and checks and fixes its own work before uploading, and the mirror is a one-way snapshot. With shadcn and Tailwind v4, the key steps are an entry file with type definitions, a compiled stylesheet with safelisted layout utilities, fonts listed in extraFonts, and a conventions file. Storybook is optional, but it provides the reference that makes the sync verifiable.

item.title: Google has the best AI money can buy. Its products still feel broken (4 minute read)
item.description: Google's AI-powered search is eroding trust not because Gemini is inherently incapable, but because probabilistic answers have been inserted into an interface that users expect to deliver deterministic, verifiable results without clearly communicating uncertainty. The deeper problem may be organizational: weak feedback loops between product teams and real users can produce fragmented features optimized for internal goals rather than actual workflows. For teams integrating AI, the key is to distinguish surfaces where occasional mistakes are acceptable from those where accuracy is fundamental, while preserving direct user feedback and making uncertainty visible.

item.title: MOKSi gives GiftTrees the confidence to be both good and profitable (5 minute read)
item.description: GiftTrees worked with MOKSi to reposition itself as a profitable business that creates positive environmental and social impact, centered on the proposition “impact made easy” and an intentionally upbeat, anti-guilt tone. The refreshed identity combines a leaf-and-bow logo, expressive typography, green with vibrant purple, orange, and red, and positive imagery to distinguish the company from traditional charity and sustainability branding. The result gives GiftTrees a clearer way to unite people, planet, and profit while supporting its ambition to scale from more than five million trees planted toward one billion.

item.title: Inca Kola rebrands as the world's other cola war heats up (3 minute read)
item.description: Inca Kola simplified its identity in 2016 by removing elements such as Peru's silhouette and its founding date, creating a cleaner, more modern logo but prompting criticism that the brand is losing some of its distinctly Peruvian character. Rather than relying on explicit national symbols, the new system emphasizes belonging through imagery of social gatherings and food, while turning the logo's distinctive shape into a flexible framing device. The identity also expands into sound with a four-note mnemonic created from traditional glass cola bottles, reinforcing familiar brand associations while modernizing the overall experience.

item.title: When Chat is the Wrong UI (6 minute read)
item.description: Chat has stayed the default way to work with AI for three years, but it suits people who don't know what they want, not those who do. In the GitHub Copilot app, a canvas is a small full-stack application, with no browser chrome, that talks back and forth with the agent. Examples include a playable Connect 4 game, a local package manager, and a workflow tool that automates research and planning so a developer can step back.

item.title: Easter Eggs in Product Design & Web Design (5 minute read)
item.description: Hidden features and secret interactions make a product feel delightful and memorable, tapping into the dopamine hit of discovering something unexpected.

item.title: The Death of Web Development Education (8 minute read)
item.description: Generative AI has gutted the market for web-development education.

item.title: At Meta Connect, the company's smart glasses were everywhere (4 minute read)
item.description: At Meta Connect, hands-on demos showed how Meta's smart glasses could support everyday tasks through its upcoming Muse integration, from sending emails to reading to-do lists aloud. The assistant still struggled to distinguish commands from nearby conversation, highlighting a challenge for voice-driven interfaces. Meta also demonstrated a separate $150 pair designed for people with hearing loss, with adjustable amplification that focuses on the person ahead or picks up sound from all directions.

item.title: Lovable's Annualized Revenue Crosses $600M as Vibe Coding Takes Off (2 minute read)
item.description: Lovable's annualized revenue has crossed $600 million, up from roughly $500 million in June. Two-thirds of Fortune 500 companies now use the vibe-coding platform, whose customers include Microsoft, Nvidia, and Deutsche Telekom. Apps built on Lovable draw nearly a billion monthly views, and two funding rounds totaling over $700 million lifted its valuation to $13.3 billion.

item.title: Apple adds RAW support for 11 digital cameras across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple has expanded RAW image support across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, adding compatibility for 11 more Fujifilm, OM System, Panasonic, and Phase One cameras, bringing the total number of supported models to 562.

item.title: Code as the Source of Truth (2 minute read)
item.description: With AI tooling, treating code as the shared source of truth lets design and engineering function as one real team rather than handing work off in sequence. Designers can prototype real coded components before engineers finalize them, while engineers push directly into Figma for designers to refine, provided a subject-matter expert reviews every step. Pairing engineers and designers to teach each other's practices speeds up delivery, and, over time, the title lines between them begin to blur.

item.title: Brand as Software (19 minute read)
item.description: In-house brand teams have become service desks: at Ramp, a Slack help channel logged more than 375 requests in six months. Brand as software carries a company's point of view, product truths, and design decisions into the work itself, with artists setting the bar and builders codifying it. A Slack agent there already turns an attached doc into a near-final deck in one pass, so designers spend time on work no system can predict.

item.title: Apple's perfect iPhone Duo TikToks nail foldable phone marketing (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple is leaning into playful, social-first marketing for the iPhone Duo with a series of TikTok sketches that showcase the foldable's versatility in everyday scenarios, from a mini laptop to a portable movie screen. Unlike Apple's typically minimalist campaigns, these ads spend more time explaining the product's use cases, reflecting the challenge of introducing its first foldable into a market where rivals like Samsung, Huawei, and Honor already have years of experience.

item.title: Should UX Designers Learn to Code? (11 minute read)
item.description: Whether UX designers should learn to code depends on context: knowing a product's technical materials speeds up workflows and suits lean, bootstrapped teams. Yet coding can invite scope creep, narrow thinking toward technical constraints, and waste time on languages that quickly become obsolete. Teams with more T-shaped members, deep in one field and broadly aware of others, communicate more easily and ship better products faster.

item.title: That Crisp Interface is Going to Date (5 minute read)
item.description: Today's crisp interfaces, with generous white space and a single decisive CTA, will date the way drop shadows and gradients did. Software has never been cheaper to ship, yet it keeps yielding identical landing pages, and AI models serving up the center of the distribution make it worse. Gumroad, Are.na, Substack, and Nothing show the alternative: someone had a default available and chose something else, from oversized type to deliberate friction.

item.title: From YWCA to Hotel Willo: how Rethink solved one of branding's trickiest problems (5 minute read)
item.description: Hotel Willo rebranded a Vancouver hotel to overcome outdated perceptions tied to its former YWCA identity, replacing the name with a fresh, approachable brand centered on a simple willow-inspired logo. The identity uses restrained design, playful messaging, and consistent applications to communicate an affordable, welcoming boutique hotel while clearly distancing it from past misconceptions.

item.title: Illustrator Rosa Snijders Finds the Softness in Grief, Debt, and All of Life's Heavy Subjects (6 minute read)
item.description: Dutch illustrator Rosa Snijders built an editorial career drawing heavy subjects like grief and death for outlets including Le Monde, National Geographic, and Corriere della Sera, using soft palettes rather than grim imagery.

item.title: Seven Artists Reveal the Revelations That Took Their Practice to the Next Level (7 minute read)
item.description: Seven artists describe the realizations that took their practice further, from building faces out of geometric forms to dropping the idea of being a watercolor purist.

item.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses (3 minute read)
item.description: Meta introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, camera-free AI glasses that support music, calls, speech translation, and its Muse assistant, offering an alternative to smart glasses that can record people without their consent. Removing the cameras makes the frames slimmer and lighter at 43 grams, with adjustable temple tips, swappable nose pads, and a battery life of up to 12 hours. Starting at $349, the glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles with prescription options.

item.title: macOS 27 gives you more control over Liquid Glass (3 minute read)
item.description: macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a customizable Liquid Glass appearance slider that lets users adjust the system's transparency from highly clear to more opaque, changing the look of the Dock, widgets, sidebars, toolbars, and apps like Music and Podcasts with a single system-wide setting. The update gives users more control over the Mac's visual style while preserving the modern Liquid Glass design language.

item.title: Adobe Premiere, One of the iPhone's Best Video-Editing Apps, is Now on Android (3 minute read)
item.description: Adobe is bringing its redesigned Premiere video-editing app to Android, nearly a year after its iPhone debut, replacing Premiere Rush, which loses support September 30. Layouts adapt across devices, pairing footage and a multitrack timeline side by side on foldables while still running on candy-bar phones like the Pixel. The app is free with no login required, though Firefly-powered features like Generative Fill require paid generative credits once the monthly allotment runs out.

item.title: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design (8 minute read)
item.description: As more interface work turns AI-generated, research and design output shifts from human-facing deliverables toward curated context that guides AI, dubbed UX-context design. DESIGN.md, which Google Labs open-sourced in April 2026 from its Stitch tool, encodes a product's visual identity for AI tools in exact values and plain-language guidance. A hypothetical broader file, UX.md, would add research findings, interaction standards, a glossary, and user and world models as a continuously updated source.

item.title: Modernizing a legacy system? Your before/after isn't the case study (5 minute read)
item.description: Strong modernization case studies focus less on before-and-after visuals and more on the design decisions behind them, highlighting the judgment calls that shaped the final product rather than the process or visual refresh alone. Employers want to understand what changed because of the designer's thinking, not just that an outdated interface now looks modern.

item.title: Nothing has changed other than how we talk about it (8 minute read)
item.description: Agentic AI can dramatically speed up the research and problem-definition phases of Design Thinking by analyzing assumptions, synthesizing evidence, and pressure-testing ideas, but human judgment remains essential for validating outputs and making design decisions. Rather than replacing designers, AI shifts their role from generating information to evaluating evidence, challenging assumptions, and deciding what should be built.

item.title: Design Systems are a Collection of Decisions (10 minute read)
item.description: Design systems amount to collections of already-made decisions, so mechanical checks can prove straight from the artifact whether an AI agent used real components and correct tokens. Judgment-based evals still have an answer key when the system has documented a decision, like a required confirmation pattern for destructive actions. Visual evals work against a known reference, but deciding whether a new visual direction deserves to exist should stay with people.

item.title: Spatial UI Design: Tips and Best Practices (21 minute read)
item.description: Augmented reality design differs from screen-based UX, demanding attention to physical space, bodily comfort, and the cognitive load added to real-world distractions. UX consultant Frank Spillers' guidelines favor real-world physics, direct hand gestures over menus, context-aware triggers, and short, interruptible interactions. Content should stay within about 30 degrees of a user's central field of view, never past 50, and sit between 1.25 and 5 meters away.
